license_notes: Manufacturer datasheet and manufacturer-distributed SPICE model, redistributed here unmodified for engineering traceability only. Copyright remains with Semiconductor Components Industries, LLC; the model file carries a Fairchild Semiconductor attribution line, reproduced unaltered.
why_this_part: Two 1N4148 form the negative-rail bias reference of the gain block (circuits/preamp/gain_block.py:252-253, footprint FP_DO35 = Diode_THT:D_DO-35_SOD27_P7.62mm_Horizontal). It is the only diode in the signal-path bias chain and it had NEVER been verified by anyone - ADR-016 lists it as 'mai verificato'.
the_part_was_not_substituted_it_was_ATTR: 1N4148 is a generic industry type number, not one manufacturer's part. T7 is therefore satisfied not by replacing the device but by naming the manufacturer whose model and lifecycle statement the project stands on. That manufacturer is onsemi, chosen because it publishes BOTH a reachable SPICE model and an explicit Active status for the DO-35 part - Vishay's 1N4148 datasheet is reachable (Rev. 1.6, 07-Nov-2024, https://www.vishay.com/docs/81857/1n4148.pdf) but its product page offers no SPICE model, only third-party ECAD models via UltraLibrarian.

why_both_files_are_named_1N914_and_not_1.short: Because at onsemi the 1N4148 is documented and modelled under the 1N914 family, and the file that IS named for our part is for a different part.
why_both_files_are_named_1N914_and_not_1.the_trap: https://www.onsemi.com/download/models/lib/1n4148.lib returns a real file (1189 bytes, application/octet-stream) - and its content is '.SUBCKT 1N4148WT', the SOD-323 surface-mount variant, generated by 'ON MPD, Multi Market Power Division', 2024, 'Rev0: Initial release of PSPICE model for 1N4148WT'. It is NOT the DO-35 part this design uses. The identical file is also served as 1n4148wt.lib (same 1189 bytes), which confirms the alias.
why_both_files_are_named_1N914_and_not_1.the_file_that_is_right: 1n914.lib declares in its own header: '** Product: 1N/FDLL914/A/B / 916/A/B / 4148 / 4448' and '** Package: DO-35 / LL-34'. It explicitly covers the 4148 in the package this design uses.
why_both_files_are_named_1N914_and_not_1.the_confirmation_that_closes_it: onsemi's own 1N4148 product page links exactly ONE datasheet, and that datasheet is /download/data-sheet/pdf/1n914-d.pdf. So the manufacturer itself files the 1N4148 under the 1N914 document. Falsifiable with: grep -o '/download/data-sheet/pdf/[a-z0-9-]*\.pdf' on the saved product page - the only match is 1n914-d.pdf.
why_both_files_are_named_1N914_and_not_1.why_it_is_recorded_here: This is the L7 lesson one level up. L7 found that a file's NAME is not its REVISION. Here a file's name is not its PART. Both fail silently: ngspice loads 1n4148.lib without complaint and simulates a different device.

revision_note: Read from the DOCUMENT FOOTER, not the filename: 'September, 2024 - Rev. 6', publication order number 1N914/D. Document title: 'Small Signal Diode - 1N91x, 1N4x48, FDLL914, FDLL4x48'. Falsifiable with: /opt/homebrew/bin/pdftotext -layout 1n914-d.pdf - | grep -i 'Rev. 6'

limits_read_with_their_conditions.V_F: 1.0 V MAXIMUM at IF = 10 mA, TA = 25 C - the row labelled '914 / 916 / 4148'. NOTE that the same table gives 0.62/0.72 V at IF = 5.0 mA for the 914B/4448 grades, which are DIFFERENT parts; reading the wrong row here would import a tighter window than this part carries.
limits_read_with_their_conditions.C_T: 4.0 pF MAXIMUM at VR = 0, f = 1.0 MHz - the row '914/914A/914B/4148'. (The 916 group is 2.0 pF; again, a different row.)
limits_read_with_their_conditions.t_rr: 4.0 ns maximum at IF = 10 mA, VR = 6.0 V, Irr = 1.0 mA, RL = 100 ohm.
limits_read_with_their_conditions.V_R_breakdown: 100 V minimum. THE TEST CURRENT COULD NOT BE READ MECHANICALLY - see the extraction warning below - and it is not a design constraint here anyway: the two diodes sit across roughly 1.3 V in the bias chain.
limits_read_with_their_conditions.package: DO-204AH (DO-35), bulk, marking '4148' - read from the ORDERING INFORMATION table, which lists 1N4148, 1N4148TA, 1N4148-T26A, 1N4148-T50A, 1N4148TR and 1N4148-T50R, all DO-204AH. This matches FP_DO35 in gain_block.py.

extraction_warning_that_applies_to_every.what: pdftotext renders the micro prefix of THIS VENDOR'S PDFs as the letter 'm'. A current read mechanically is therefore wrong by a factor of 1000, with exit code 0 and no warning.
extraction_warning_that_applies_to_every.proved_how: The rendered page shows 'Pulse Width = 1.0 us' with a real micro glyph; pdftotext -layout returns 'Pulse Width = 1.0 ms' for the same row. Counting the glyph across four datasheets: 1n914-d.pdf 0, mje15032-d.pdf 0, the already-frozen 2n5551t-d.pdf 0, and the Linear Systems LSK489 datasheet 11. So it is a property of onsemi's document toolchain, not of poppler. The nano prefix survives, which is what makes it dangerous: spot-checking a row that uses 'n' says the extraction is fine.
extraction_warning_that_applies_to_every.consequence_here: The IR and VR test currents in this datasheet's ELECTRICAL CHARACTERISTICS come out as 'mA' where the document says microamps. They are not used by this project, and they are recorded as unread rather than transcribed wrong.

lifecycle.verbatim_from_manufacturer: Read on 2026-09-10 from the JSON-LD offers/itemProductList block on onsemi's own product page: 1N4148 -> 'Active' / 'available' / $0.0073; 1N4148TA -> Active/available; 1N4148TR -> Active/available; 1N4148-T26A -> Active/available; 1N4148-T50A -> Active/available; 1N4148-T50R -> Active/unavailable. Six OPNs, all Active.
lifecycle.not_from_a_distributor: A web search returned 'Active' for this part from Octopart, DigiKey, Sourcengine and TrustedParts. Those were NOT used: T8 says the lifecycle is read from the manufacturer, and that rule exists because the THAT320's EOL memo had been public for a week while the distributor picture still looked healthy.

spice_model.status: FOUND, served by the manufacturer, and PROVEN to load and run in ngspice.
spice_model.authorship_declared_in_the_file: '** Creation: Jul-24-2007 Rev: 1.0 ** Fairchild Semiconductor'. Fairchild was acquired by onsemi in 2016 and onsemi serves the file today from its own host, which is what ADR-016 freezes.

datasheet_cross_check_L24.V_F_at_IF_10mA_25C: MEASURED 0.76619 V against a datasheet MAXIMUM of 1.0 V. Inside, with 23% of margin.
datasheet_cross_check_L24.V_F_at_the_design_point_1mA_25C: MEASURED 0.63195 V. No published window at this current; this is the number that actually sets the negative-rail bias reference.
datasheet_cross_check_L24.C_T_at_VR_0_1MHz_25C: MEASURED 0.8687 pF against a datasheet MAXIMUM of 4.0 pF. Inside, but note it is 4.6x BELOW the guaranteed ceiling - the model carries CJO = 0.868 pF, i.e. it describes a typical-or-better sample rather than the worst case the datasheet allows. For a bias-reference diode carrying 1 mA this does not matter; it would matter if this diode were ever put in a signal path.
datasheet_cross_check_L24.verdict: CONFORMING on both published limits. No mixed verdict here, unlike the LSK489 (NC-013) and unlike MJE15032.
